video.title: Watch Me Build an AI Agency in 24 Minutes

summary: Chris Koerner builds a sample AI voice agent for roofing contractors, scrapes local business listings, and tests a cold-text campaign to find potential customers. The agent answers common roofing questions and offers to schedule a roof inspection; the video does not show a paying customer or a completed sale. Koerner reports replies and warm leads from a 100-contact experiment, then estimates what those results might mean at larger volumes. He also recommends testing several local-business industries and promotes his AI implementation community.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office; also identifies himself in the video as Chris.

ideas.name: Custom AI voice agents for roofing contractors
ideas.one_liner: Build and configure a branded phone agent that answers roofing questions and helps callers arrange inspections.
ideas.business_model: Recurring monthly service or subscription; Koerner expects customers may pay for the service but reports no closed sale in this experiment.
ideas.customer: Roofing contractors, initially those in the Dallas–Fort Worth area.
ideas.problem: Roofers may miss calls and lose quote or inspection opportunities; they already spend on marketing services and want more jobs.
ideas.offer: A customized, local-number voice agent that answers calls 24/7, responds to common roofing questions, and offers inspection appointments. Koerner first creates a sample, then proposes personalizing it for an interested roofer.

pricing.model: Potential monthly fee, with a free limited-call demonstration or trial suggested.

price_points.label: Hundreds or thousands of dollars; stated as an expected possible price, not a sale.
Hypothetical monthly price used in revenue math.

pricing.notes: No actual customer price, paid contract, or close is shown. Koerner says the free agent could lead to payment for more custom work.

acquisition_channels.details: Used Outscraper to search Google Business Profile categories for roofing contractors across Dallas, Fort Worth, Plano, and Frisco, including a less commonly targeted roofing-service category. Filtered for phone numbers and later mobile numbers.

quote.text: I'm going to look for roofers. Why roofer? Well, they tend to be more tech-savvy.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Exported and randomized 100 business contacts, then sent individually customized texts from an iPhone and Mac using Straight Text. The transcript does not establish consent. UK PECR makes this approach unsuitable for unsolicited marketing texts to individuals and sole traders without consent.

quote.text: I'm going to only text 100 of them. We'll see if that does anything.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.delivery: Koerner creates a voice agent in GoHighLevel, selects a voice and local phone number, writes a roofing knowledge base with ChatGPT, and inserts business-specific details after a prospect agrees to test it. The agent handles calls and can offer appointments; the roofer would perform the physical inspection and roofing work. No paid customer onboarding or live customer delivery is demonstrated.
unit_economics_claims: The agent model is quoted at $0.02 per minute, with usage costs passed through.
The Outscraper lead pull is estimated to cost $1.50–$10.
Koerner suggests a $1,000 monthly price in a hypothetical revenue calculation; no sale is reported.
Koerner reports 15 replies and three warm leads from 96 delivered texts in this experiment.
ideas.startup_cost: The lead pull was estimated at $1.50–$10. GoHighLevel voice usage was quoted at $0.02 per minute. Other setup costs were not stated.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: No paying customer or revenue is shown. Koerner reports obtaining warm leads during the experiment, but does not report when or whether any paid revenue followed.

acquisition.how: The demonstrated channel is unsolicited text outreach, which cannot be automated legally in the UK for individuals and sole traders without consent. A compliant inbound channel or appropriately screened business outreach would be needed.

onboarding.how: Lead lists and templates can be prepared with software, but a person still needs to confirm the customer, add accurate business details, and configure the agent.

delivery.how: The voice agent can answer routine calls and offer appointments on its own, but a person must build and check its knowledge base and the contractor must perform inspections and roofing work.

billing.how: The transcript gives no billing workflow. A recurring charge could be automated, but the service and usage charges would need human setup and oversight.

support.how: Call transcripts and ratings can help review performance, but a person would need to handle incorrect answers, customer-specific changes, and escalations.

uk_applicability.notes: The voice-agent service could work for UK roofing firms, with UK-specific business details and call handling. The demonstrated unsolicited SMS prospecting is not suitable for UK individuals and sole traders without consent under PECR; local consent and data-protection requirements would need to shape acquisition.

risks: Unsolicited marketing texts to UK individuals and sole traders without consent create a PECR compliance risk.
The demo agent gives generic or potentially invented business information, including claiming the company has served the area for years; inaccurate answers could harm a roofer's reputation.
The sample knowledge base and appointment flow are not shown to be checked against a real contractor's services, availability, or service area.
Voice usage and model costs can rise with call volume or long calls.
Roofers may receive heavy marketing outreach; Koerner says competition varies by area.
The reported campaign produced warm leads, not confirmed sales, so the revenue projections remain unproven.

ideas.name: Small-business AI implementation consulting
ideas.one_liner: Help small businesses implement AI and automation, potentially on a recurring monthly basis.
ideas.business_model: Consulting or implementation service, with monthly fees suggested but not documented as actual sales.
ideas.customer: Small businesses seeking help implementing AI; Koerner specifically pitches the opportunity to people starting an AI implementation or automation business.
ideas.problem: Small businesses may need help choosing and implementing AI tools and automations.
ideas.offer: AI implementation or automation consulting. The video gives a roofing voice agent as a concrete example, but does not detail a broader consulting package.

pricing.model: Potential monthly consulting or implementation fees.

price_points.label: Thousands of dollars, suggested as a possible monthly fee.

pricing.notes: This is presented as an opportunity and promotional claim, not as a documented consulting contract.

ideas.delivery: The transcript does not describe a general consulting delivery process. Koerner demonstrates building one AI voice agent and promotes Playmakers AI as a community for people starting an implementation or automation business.
unit_economics_claims: Koerner says small businesses could pay thousands of dollars a month for AI implementation or consulting.

acquisition.how: The transcript gives no acquisition process for general consulting; inbound content and referrals could be automated partly, but no such channel is demonstrated.

onboarding.how: Consulting needs discovery of each customer's systems and needs, which usually requires human work; the video gives no automated onboarding process.

delivery.how: Some implementation work can use AI tools, but broader consulting needs a person to scope, configure, and validate solutions.

billing.how: No billing workflow is described; recurring invoices could be automated with routine oversight.

support.how: The transcript gives no support model for consulting clients; implementation changes and advice would require human involvement.

uk_applicability.notes: AI implementation consulting can serve UK small businesses, though the transcript provides no UK customer evidence or local compliance detail.

risks: The opportunity and monthly-fee claims are promotional and are not backed here by contracts, customer results, or delivery economics.
A broad consulting offer can become bespoke, increasing human delivery and support time.

tactics.name: Find a less crowded local-business segment
steps: Use Outscraper to inspect Google Business Profile categories, including less common categories that contractors may have selected by mistake.
Target multiple nearby cities and zip codes so the outreach list is geographically relevant.
Check how much marketing competition exists in the chosen niche before committing to it.

quote.text: These are categories that other dirty marketers like myself are not targeting.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Prepare and clean a local prospect list
steps: Require a phone number when scraping the listings.
Remove duplicate phone numbers, then filter to mobile numbers.
Remove business names that look unprofessional for the planned personalization.
Fill missing city fields with a local area label.
Randomize the list before choosing a sample so the contacts do not all come from one city.

quote.text: I want to perfectly randomize it by doing the formula equals rand open and then close parentheses
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Build a reusable voice-agent template, then personalize it after interest
steps: Create a sample agent with a temporary business name and a concise roofing FAQ knowledge base.
Use ChatGPT to draft the FAQ structure, then add it as rich text in GoHighLevel.
Keep business name and location as easy-to-replace variables.
Set call limits and response behavior to manage usage and reduce the risk of unusually long calls.
After a roofer agrees to test it, add that firm's actual details and a local phone number.
Test the call, inspect the transcript, and rate the result.

quote.text: I'm not going to send the roofer the link or the phone number to this AI voice agent until I have a roofer say yes.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Use a low-friction demonstration to start the sales conversation
steps: Tell prospects the agent is custom-built for their business.
Offer a free demonstration or limited number of calls to get a prospect to try it.
Use the demo as a path to discuss more customized paid work.
Respond to requests for company information with the business name and website.

quote.text: I just want to get them to respond and to try it.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Track the whole outreach funnel and compare niches
steps: Record the number of contacts, delivered texts, responses, and warm leads.
Track whether prospects are receptive, angry, or unable to pay.
Test the same offer in three to five industries, then focus on the one showing the most promise.
Treat a small sample's response rate as an early signal, not proof of revenue.

quote.text: Keep track of every single response, what your response rates are, what the sentiment is like.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Adjust the first message to sound like a customer inquiry
steps: Review whether a highly personalized message makes the sender sound like a marketer.
Test a shorter question about whether the roofer inspects roofs.
Where appropriate, use the recipient's actual first name rather than only the business name.

quote.text: I should have said something like, "Hey, do you inspect roofs? - Chris."
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

evidence_quality.rationale: The host demonstrates his own prospecting and agent-building process and reports concrete campaign counts, but no roofing customer purchase, recurring revenue, or independently verified outcomes are shown. Several revenue and conversion figures are projections from a small sample, and the lead totals are inconsistent.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Koerner promotes Playmakers AI, his AI implementation community, and an affiliate link for GoHighLevel. He also identifies Repeat Leads as his business.
